##1. Load and verify the data 
```{r}
bank <- read.csv("UniversalBank.csv")

bank

summary(bank)

table(bank$Personal.Loan)
```

##2. Remove ID and ZIP Code as predictors as instructed
##new data frame
```{r}
bank2 <- bank[,!(names(bank) %in% c("ID","ZIP.Code"))]

##check whether the predictors are properly removed
names(bank2)
```

##3. Transform categorical preditor(s) with more than 2 categories into dummy VARs
##Namely "Educ" in the data frame has 3 distinct categories
```{r}
bank2$Education <- factor(bank2$Education)

bank2 <- cbind(
  bank2[, !(names(bank2) %in% "Education")],
  model.matrix(~ Education - 1, data = bank2)
  )

##Verify VARs
names(bank2)
##Newly added: Educ1, Educ2, Educ3
```

##4. Separate the predictors and the intended target
##Only want to know the output of loan approval - VAR = Personal.Loan
```{r}
x <- bank2[, names(bank2) !="Personal.Loan"]
y <- bank2$Personal.Loan
## x = predictors; y = target/output
```

##5. Load KNN package
```{r}
library(class)
```

##6. Partition the data frame into 60% 'Training' & 40% 'Validation'
```{r}
##standardize the predictors, so everything is weighted equally in the model
x_scaled <- scale(x)

##60/40 split
##set seed so the random split is reproducible for the model, no fluctuation
library(caret)

set.seed(123)

train_index <- createDataPartition(y, p = 0.60, list = F)

x_train <- x_scaled[train_index, ]
x_valid <- x_scaled[-train_index, ]

y_train <- y[train_index]
y_valid <- y[-train_index]

##check whether the split is done properly; 5000 obs 3000(60)/2000(40) 
nrow(x_train)
nrow(x_valid)
```

##7. Consider the following customer
##Specify new customer parameter
```{r}
new_customer <- data.frame(
  Age = 40,
  Experience = 10,
  Income = 84,
  Family = 2,
  CCAvg = 2,
  Mortgage = 0,
  Securities.Account = 0,
  CD.Account = 0,
  Online = 1,
  CreditCard = 1,
  Education1 = 0,
  Education2 = 1,
  Education3 = 0
)

##scale new_customer, so it fits into scaled predictors
new_customer_scaled <- scale(
  new_customer,
  center = attr(x_scaled, "scaled:center"),
  scale = attr(x_scaled, "scaled:scale")
)

customer_pred <- knn(
  train = x_train,
  test = new_customer_scaled,
  cl = factor(y_train),
  k = 1
)

##verify prediction
customer_pred
```

##8. Find K-value that balances between overfitting and ignoring predictor info
##Most fitting/best K-value
```{r}
##test different k-values, from 1 to 50
k_values <- 1:50

accuracy <- numeric(length(k_values))

for (i in seq_along(k_values)) {
  pred <- knn(
    train = x_train,
    test = x_valid,
    cl = factor(y_train),
    k = k_values[i]
  )

##compare predictions with validation results  
  accuracy[i] <- mean(pred == factor(y_valid))
}

##table for each k-value and corresponding validation accuracy
k_results <- data.frame(
  k = k_values,
  Accuracy = accuracy
)

k_results

##find the best k-value
k_best <- k_results$k[which.max(k_results$Accuracy)]

k_best

##visual for better comparison
plot(
  k_results$k,
  k_results$Accuracy,
  type = "b",
  xlab = "k",
  ylab = "Validation Accuracy",
  main = "k-NN: Validation Accuracy"
)
```

##9. Confusion matrix
```{r}
pred_best <- knn(
  train = x_train,
  test = x_valid,
  cl = factor(y_train),
  k = k_best
)

confusion_valid <- table(
  Actual = y_valid,
  Predicted = pred_best
)

confusion_valid
```

##10. Check accuracy of the matrix
```{r}
mean(pred_best == factor(y_valid))
```


##11. Classify customer using the best k-value
```{r}
customer_best <- knn(
  train = x_train,
  test = new_customer_scaled,
  cl = factor(y_train),
  k = k_best
)

customer_best

##R should return either 0 or 1; 0 being 'not accepting loan', 1 being ' accepting loan'
```

##12. Repartition the data into 'Training', 'Validation', 'Test'
```{r}
##set seed so random split is reproducible for the new model
set.seed(123)

##first splitting data into 50% training and 50% pending for partition: validation (30); testing (20)
train_index2 <- createDataPartition(y, p = 0.50, list = F)

x_train2 <- x_scaled[train_index2, ]
X_remaining2 <- x_scaled[-train_index2, ]

y_train2 <- y[train_index2]
y_remaining2 <- y[-train_index2]

validation_index2 <- createDataPartition(y_remaining2, p = 0.60, list = F)

x_valid2 <- X_remaining2[validation_index2, ]
x_test2 <- X_remaining2[-validation_index2, ]

y_valid2 <- y_remaining2[validation_index2]
y_test2 <- y_remaining2[-validation_index2]

##verify whether the data is properly divided
##50% of 5000 = 2500
nrow(x_train2)
##30% of 5K = 1500
nrow(x_valid2)
##20% of 5K = 1000
nrow(x_test2)
```

##13. Apply KNN method with best k-value(k_best)
```{r}
pred_train2 <- knn(
  train = x_train2,
  test = x_train2,
  cl = factor(y_train2),
  k = k_best
)

pred_valid2 <- knn(
  train = x_train2,
  test = x_valid2,
  cl = factor(y_train2),
  k = k_best
)

pred_test2 <- knn(
  train = x_train2,
  test = x_test2,
  cl = factor(y_train2),
  k = k_best
)

pred_train2
pred_valid2
pred_test2
```

##14. Confusion matrix for the datasets
```{r}
con_train <- table(
  Actual = y_train2,
  Predicted = pred_train2
)

con_train

con_valid <- table(
  Actual = y_valid2,
  Predicted = pred_valid2
)

con_valid

con_test <- table(
  Actual = y_test2,
  Predicted = pred_test2
)

con_test
```

##15. Check accuracy of the matrix 
```{r}
accuracy_train <- mean(pred_train2 == factor(y_train2))

accuracy_valid <- mean(pred_valid2 == factor(y_valid2))

accuracy_test <- mean(pred_test2 == factor(y_test2))

accuracy_comparison <- c(
  Training = accuracy_train,
  Validation = accuracy_valid,
  Test = accuracy_test
)

accuracy_comparison
```

##The 'Training' accuracy is 100%, while 'Validation' accuracy is 95.7% and 'Test' accuracy were is 96.4%. The higher accuracy in 'Training' is expected because the model is trained on the given observations, whereas 'Validation' and 'Test' are lower because they contain observations that the model is not trained on these observations. The difference between 'Training' and 'Validation'/'Test' suggests some overfitting; however, given how similar the 'Validation' accuracy is to the 'Test' accuracy, the overfitting issue is not severe and the model generalizes well to unseen data.
